one_line: Shared quote editor for Italian tradespeople and AI agents.
what_it_does: Builds VAT-aware material quotes with agent-assisted catalog search, line-item edits, margin review, and human finalization.
leverage_rationale: Typed tools operate on shared quote state and expose structured calculations, undo, permissions, and recoverable errors; UI driving would be materially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Description lists granular quote tools and live highlighted/undoable actions.
Screenshot visibly shows line items, VAT totals, margin warning, and WebMCP panel.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent central workflow and the screenshot shows a populated quote through finalization controls, though no transcript and limited frame clarity reduce certainty.
execution_evidence: Visible quote includes customer, material rows, subtotal, VAT, total, margin, and Finalize Quote.
Implementation claims polyfill, permissions, activity feed, and Italian VAT handling.
impact_rationale: Italian artisans have a concrete high-stakes quoting problem involving repetitive entry, tax correctness, and margin errors.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies idraulico, elettricista, and termotecnico users and specific VAT/margin pain points.
creativity_rationale: Human and agent editing the same quote with explicit oversight is a thoughtful domain-specific collaboration model.
creativity_evidence: Shared-page quote collaboration and one-click human finalization are clearly pursued.
usability_note: Quote UI and assistant activity afford review and undo; some controls are small in evidence image.
red_flags: No actual submitted video/transcript despite frame-sheet references.
standouts: VAT and recoverable-error details show care.
advance_reason: Strong leverage and credible useful workflow with visible product evidence.

one_line: Browser Pokémon recreation where humans and multiple agents share one trainer.
what_it_does: Exposes map, party, and battle state as tools so agents coordinate gameplay from semantics rather than pixels.
leverage_rationale: A pixel-only Game Boy-like surface is exceptionally difficult for agents; shared structured game state changes feasibility and coordination.
leverage_evidence: Packet explicitly contrasts state tools with pixel driving and supports many simultaneous agents.
Concept addresses coordination failures exemplified by Twitch Plays Pokémon.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete playable adaptation and shared save model, but end-to-end execution is not directly demonstrated by transcript.
execution_evidence: Live demo is alive and project claims map, party, and battle tools.
Two gallery images and three referenced frame sheets provide packaging/product evidence.
impact_rationale: It offers meaningful entertainment and experimentation value for game and agent-interaction audiences, though the use case is niche.
impact_evidence: Shared-agent gameplay directly reframes a known crowd-play experience.
creativity_rationale: The Twitch Plays Pokémon premise is recombined with semantic multi-agent collaboration in a memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Many agents sharing one trainer and communicating over readable game state is distinctive.
usability_note: Shared state may improve coordination, but simultaneous-agent conflict management is not fully evidenced.
red_flags: Built from an existing open-source Pokémon recreation; new WebMCP contribution is claimed but not independently observed.
standouts: Strong case for structured state over pixel automation.
advance_reason: Exceptional creativity and transformative leverage outweigh limited observed execution evidence.

one_line: Web spreadsheet and CSV manipulation workspace.
what_it_does: A browser app intended to let users and agents clean and edit Excel/CSV data.
leverage_rationale: Spreadsheet edits are already accessible through UI automation; the packet does not specify a distinctive structured agent capability or shared-state delta.
leverage_evidence: Pitch only says manipulate and edit Excel/CSV files.
WebMCP is listed in the technology stack without tool behavior.
execution_rationale: The submission packaging is extremely sparse and provides no video frames, transcript, or demonstrated end-to-end workflow.
execution_evidence: Only a short pitch and generic project description are provided.
No frame sheets submitted.
impact_rationale: Spreadsheet cleaning is a real, broad productivity need, but the solution's concrete scope and efficacy are unclear.
impact_evidence: Description names filtering, deduplication, and data cleaning pain points.
creativity_rationale: The concept is a conventional spreadsheet editor with an agent angle and little evidenced novelty.
creativity_evidence: No distinctive interaction model or novel workflow is described.
usability_note: Likely familiar spreadsheet interaction, but no usable flow is evidenced.
red_flags: Very thin evidence; no video frames or tool details.
advance_reason: Insufficient evidence and weakly differentiated WebMCP leverage.

one_line: Shared regulated-dossier review workspace for humans and agents.
what_it_does: Runs typed evidence checks, digest-bound checkpoints, source review, normalized corrections, and revalidation without changing source PDFs.
leverage_rationale: Digest-bound structured checks and shared evidence state are materially safer and more precise than UI scraping in regulated review.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies typed evidence bundles, immutable source bytes/digests, and digest-bound approvals.
Tools share the same documents and results as the human reviewer.
execution_rationale: The Documents-to-Findings-to-Corrections-to-Close flow is coherent and detailed, but demo availability is unknown and no video exists.
execution_evidence: Packet describes planted revision and pH disagreements and commit re-running checks.
No public repository and no submitted video.
impact_rationale: Regulated dossier reconciliation has a concrete safety and compliance audience, and immutable evidence plus human approval directly addresses its risks.
impact_evidence: Human-only approval and unchanged source PDFs are explicit safeguards.
creativity_rationale: The combination of shared review, provenance, digest binding, and agent-safe correction semantics is an original and ambitious workflow.
creativity_evidence: Agent can focus findings and open governing PDFs while preserving source integrity.
usability_note: Linear review stages and human approval boundary are promising; live access is not verified.
red_flags: Demo status unknown and no public repository or video evidence.
advance_reason: High-impact, high-leverage concept with unusually strong safety semantics despite evidence limitations.

one_line: Local-first file investigation workspace with agent-accessible privacy analysis.
what_it_does: Parses diverse files in-browser, surfaces hidden content and metadata, supports cross-file search/reasoning, and lets humans approve cleanup proposals.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives agents structured provenance-rich access to a local multi-file workspace while preserving human execution boundaries; UI scraping cannot comparably support this reliably.
leverage_evidence: Video transcript reports 17 tools, privacy scans, provenance, cross-file entities, duplicates, timelines, and human-approved proposals.
Transcript explicitly says files stay local and agents cannot execute proposed changes.
execution_rationale: The 149-second video transcript demonstrates a broad coherent workflow from loading files through scans, proposals, human actions, export, and deeper analyses.
execution_evidence: Video facts: alive demo, 149-second video.
Transcript reports concrete findings changing from 10 to 5 and 6 to 0, quarantine, export, and rollback-related analysis.
impact_rationale: Privacy-conscious users and organizations have a clear need to inspect hidden content and metadata before sharing files; local processing directly addresses trust concerns.
impact_evidence: 14-file synthetic case, hidden text/metadata/GPS/macros and prompt-injection detection are demonstrated in transcript.
creativity_rationale: The local tab as file parser and agent as cross-file investigator is a strong, memorable use of WebMCP with unusually deep coverage.
creativity_evidence: Combines hidden-content forensics, provenance, cross-file reasoning, human proposal approval, and local-only processing.
usability_note: Preview, Reveal hidden, proposal cards, and explicit human execution boundaries form a clear workflow.
red_flags: Synthetic fixtures limit evidence of production robustness.
standouts: Best-evidenced end-to-end agent workflow in this packet.
advance_reason: Outstanding demonstrated leverage, execution, impact, and originality.

one_line: Deterministic HVAC intake classification and evaluation workbench.
what_it_does: Lets agents inspect fictional intake cases, classify trade/intent/urgency, identify missing data, and score results visibly for humans.
leverage_rationale: Structured deterministic classification and scoring improve repeatability and inspectability, though a general agent could achieve similar outcomes with UI friction.
leverage_evidence: Nine tools and deterministic scorer are explicitly described.
Human-visible decisions and repeatable scoring are central.
execution_rationale: The scope is coherent but evidence is thin: no video frames, transcript, or public repository to substantiate the claimed working tools.
execution_evidence: Live demo is marked alive.
Description names fictional cases, routing, missing-information checks, and scoring.
impact_rationale: HVAC intake errors can affect urgency and routing, making this a credible service-operations use case, albeit demonstrated only with fictional cases.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies repetitive intake and consequences for service decisions.
creativity_rationale: A human-verifiable deterministic intake benchmark is a useful angle on agent evaluation, but the domain workflow is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Combines WebMCP intake tools with repeatable scoring and inspectability.
usability_note: Human-visible classifications are promising; no screenshots or observed flow support stronger judgment.
red_flags: No frame sheets or public source; evidence relies on prose claims.
standouts: Deterministic scoring is a sensible trust feature.
advance_reason: Credible idea but insufficient execution evidence and moderate differentiation.

one_line: Learns reusable agent routines from one human-agent collaboration.
what_it_does: Records semantic actions, separates variables from durable policy and examples, then replays a routine on new inputs with a human approval pause.
leverage_rationale: The shared semantic trace and deterministic routine compilation create reusable procedural memory not reliably obtainable from generic UI macros or chat history.
leverage_evidence: Human and WebMCP actions share a semantic command bus and trace.
Replay restores policy and pauses at learned approval boundary.
execution_rationale: The packet carefully bounds claims to deterministic vendor evaluation and describes a complete teach-then-run workflow, with frame sheets and gallery evidence but no transcript.
execution_evidence: Claims deterministic separation of variables, policy, procedures, outputs, and example-only corrections.
Live demo and three frame sheets are listed.
impact_rationale: Teams repeatedly re-teaching agents procedures is a real productivity problem; reusable policy with approval boundaries has credible value.
impact_evidence: Vendor evaluation MVP demonstrates recurring decision workflow and human approval requirement.
creativity_rationale: Teaching an agent once through a semantic human-agent trace, then compiling reusable routines, is a notably original interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Explicit distinction between durable rules and one-off corrections is unusually thoughtful.
usability_note: Teach this routine and approval pause provide understandable control points; arbitrary workflow generality is not claimed.
red_flags: MVP is domain-specific and uses fictional fixtures; no transcript.
standouts: Strong conceptual treatment of procedural memory and oversight.
advance_reason: Highly original, high-leverage collaboration model with a bounded credible MVP.

one_line: Shared 3D olfactory knowledge atlas for perfumer and agent reasoning.
what_it_does: Provides typed search, relation, comparison, graph-path, and visual-focus tools over an olfeme corpus without modifying evidence.
leverage_rationale: Structured graph traversal and synchronized visual focus avoid brittle canvas interpretation while keeping agent evidence and human exploration aligned.
leverage_evidence: Five bounded tools expose search, relations, comparisons, paths, and focus_nodes.
Description contrasts typed schemas with scraping a dense 3D canvas.
execution_rationale: The workflow and side-effect boundaries are coherent, but the authenticated atlas and no transcript limit observed execution confidence.
execution_evidence: Live demo marked alive and frame sheets/gallery evidence listed.
Claims corpus evidence is separated from formulation interpretation.
impact_rationale: Perfume formulation and olfactory research have a real need for interpretable retrieval and relationship tracing, though the audience is specialized.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies ambiguity in sensory language and contextual formulation problems.
creativity_rationale: The combination of olfactory graph knowledge, 3D shared context, and agent-directed visual focus is distinctive.
creativity_evidence: Agent points the perfumer to the same olfemes and graph evidence on screen.
usability_note: Narrow tools and visual focus may tame a dense atlas, but authentication and 3D complexity add friction.
red_flags: Built around an existing Crystal Neural Atlas; newness of the underlying product is unclear.
advance_reason: Distinctive research/creative application with meaningful structured-agent delta.

one_line: Agent-assisted F-1 student visa preparation and advising workspace.
what_it_does: Uses bounded tools and deterministic duration-of-status calculations to create student and DSO briefs from confirmed case facts.
leverage_rationale: Specialized structured reference and deterministic regulatory calculation let an agent coordinate intake and evidence more reliably than generic UI interaction.
leverage_evidence: Agent proposes remembered facts, asks for consequential gaps, and invokes a deterministic mapper after confirmation.
Produces coordinated source-linked student and DSO documents.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent intake-to-calculation-to-PDF workflow with live demo and multiple evidence images, but no transcript.
execution_evidence: Live demo and four gallery images are reported.
Deterministic dates/timeline and downloadable PDFs are explicitly claimed.
impact_rationale: International students face high-stakes, changing visa rules and repetitive intake; practical preparation briefs can materially improve advising readiness.
impact_evidence: Specific F-1 study, employment, travel, and compliance decisions are named.
creativity_rationale: Personal-agent memory coordinating with a specialized visa rules engine and producing two audience-specific briefs is a strong synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Agent fills only consequential gaps and separates student-facing from DSO-facing outputs.
usability_note: Confirmation and polished PDF outputs support usability; immigration-domain complexity requires careful review.
red_flags: High-stakes regulatory content is described but not independently validated in the packet.
standouts: Good human-confirmation boundary for sensitive calculations.
advance_reason: Credible high-impact domain workflow with substantial agent leverage.

one_line: Agent-assisted procurement board for supplier fit and tender integrity screening.
what_it_does: Sweeps notices, extracts criteria, scores supplier qualification, flags suspiciously narrow clauses, and produces a dated bid plan with mirrored traces.
leverage_rationale: Structured multi-document extraction and shared live ranking materially improve scale, precision, and human auditability over UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Seven tools perform autonomous sweep, criteria evaluation, integrity flags, and profile-driven reranking.
Every call, output, latency, and evidence rationale is mirrored for the human.
execution_rationale: The packet specifies a coherent one-button end-to-end sweep over twelve notices and live reranking, with multiple gallery/frame references but no transcript.
execution_evidence: Claims twelve-notice sweep, met/gap/unclear criteria, four integrity flags, and bid plan.
Live board reranks a notice from 17 to 41 after profile update.
impact_rationale: Small suppliers face a real capacity barrier in reading public tenders; qualification and integrity screening could widen participation and improve competition.
impact_evidence: Product addresses both bid/no-bid decisions and restrictive tender wording.
creativity_rationale: Combining supplier qualification with public-procurement integrity analysis in a shared agent-human board is ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: One autonomous pass produces fit reasoning, integrity flags, and a dated plan.
usability_note: One-button sweep and mirrored reasoning are clear, though dense procurement evidence may challenge new users.
red_flags: Claims rely on fictional/open notices and no transcript is supplied.
standouts: Strong social value framing around supplier access and tender integrity.
Live reranking makes shared state concrete.
advance_reason: High-impact, well-matched WebMCP workflow with strong structured reasoning and visible state.
